observation: The main friction is repeated clarification loops before any draft exists. This is concentrated in `needsMoreInfo`: 13 traversals into `needsMoreInfo`, 9 `MORE_INFO` returns to `evaluating`, and all 3 `missing-optional` runs took 3 clarification turns each before drafting. Revisions are 0, so review is not the bottleneck. The current evaluator policy also treats every gap the same: `evaluatePrompt.system` says `Require recipient, subject, and body details`, which forces optional-detail cases through the same stop-and-ask path as harder cases.
proposal: Make one bounded change to the evaluator policy so it only blocks on a valid recipient before drafting, and treats missing subject/body detail as non-blocking draftable gaps. Concretely, change the `evaluatePrompt.system` request from requiring `recipient, subject, and body details` to requiring only a valid recipient for satisfaction, while still returning questions for missing optional content that the drafter can handle. This preserves all non-negotiables: sending still only happens from `reviewing`/`finalReview` on `SEND`; every draft is still reviewed before send; and a valid recipient is still required before the machine can reach `drafting` and thus `sending`.

changes.change: Replace `Require recipient, subject, and body details. Return missing fields and one question per gap.` with guidance that only a valid recipient is mandatory to proceed, while subject/body gaps should be noted but need not make `satisfied` false. Example intent: `Evaluate an email drafting request. A valid recipient is required before drafting. If recipient is missing or invalid, return satisfied=false and ask for it. Missing subject/body detail may be returned as questions, but should not block drafting when a recipient is present.`

keeps: Keep `needsMoreInfo` and `DRAFT_ANYWAY`; recipient-missing cases can still stop there.
Keep `SEND` as the only path to `sending`.
Keep the valid-recipient requirement before sending by enforcing it in evaluation.
measure: Success metric: reduce clarification turns and model calls in `missing-optional` runs. Specifically, expect the `complete` path shape (`evaluating > drafting > reviewing > sending > sent`) to absorb most `missing-optional` cases, cutting their clarificationTurns from 3 toward 0 and modelCalls from 4 toward 2, while leaving sendRuleViolations at 0.
